unit.title: Temporal Clauses: Indicative vs Subjunctive
unit.subtitle: cuando, en cuanto, hasta que and the pull of the future

grammar.title: When ‘when’ hasn't happened yet
grammar.intro: Temporal connectors like cuando, en cuanto, hasta que and mientras switch mood depending on when the action happens. If it's habitual or already realized, use the indicative: Cuando llego a casa, ceno. If it's anticipated and not yet realized, use the subjunctive: Cuando llegues, llámame. Getting this right is what separates a fluent speaker from a merely competent one.

sections.heading: Realized → indicative; pending → subjunctive
sections.body: A single connector takes either mood. Ask: has the action already happened (or does it happen habitually)? Then indicative. Is it still to come, viewed from the moment of speaking? Then subjunctive — never the future tense inside the clause.

ex.es: En cuanto termino de comer, friego los platos.
ex.en: As soon as I finish eating, I wash the dishes.

ex.es: En cuanto termine el informe, te lo mando.
ex.en: As soon as I finish the report, I'll send it to you.

sections.heading: The temporal connectors
sections.body: These all follow the same rule. Mientras also means ‘as long as’ (condition) with the subjunctive. Siempre que is temporal (‘whenever’) with the indicative for habits, but conditional (‘provided that’) with the subjunctive.

ex.es: No me iré hasta que me digas la verdad.
ex.en: I won't leave until you tell me the truth.

ex.es: Una vez que lo hayas leído, hablamos.
ex.en: Once you've read it, we'll talk.

sections.heading: ‘antes de que’ vs ‘antes de’ + infinitive
sections.body: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, regardless of time, because the second action is by definition not yet real. But when both actions share the same subject, Spanish prefers antes de + infinitive. The same goes for después de.

ex.es: Recoge todo antes de que vuelvan tus padres.
ex.en: Tidy everything up before your parents get back.
Before leaving, I turned off the lights.

takeaways: Same connector, two moods: realized/habitual → indicative; pending/future → subjunctive.
Never put the future tense inside the temporal clause: Cuando llegues (not llegarás).
antes de que ALWAYS takes the subjunctive.
Same subject? Prefer antes de / después de + infinitive over the que clause.

mistakes.why: A pending future action inside a temporal clause takes the subjunctive, not the future tense: llegues.
The arrival hasn't happened yet, so hasta que needs the subjunctive: vengas.

mistakes.w: Llámame antes de que salgo de casa.
mistakes.r: Llámame antes de que salga de casa.
mistakes.why: antes de que always takes the subjunctive: salga, not salgo.

exercises.prompt: Te llamo en cuanto ___ a la oficina. (llegar, yo)
exercises.prompt_en: I'll call you as soon as I get to the office.
exercises.no: The arrival is still to come, so the temporal clause takes the subjunctive: “llegue”.

exercises.prompt: Todos los días, cuando ___ del trabajo, saco al perro.
exercises.prompt_en: Every day, when I get home from work, I walk the dog.
exercises.no: This is a daily habit, so use the indicative: “vuelvo”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “Tidy up before your parents get back.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! antes de que → siempre subjuntivo: vuelvan.
exercises.no: “Recoge antes de que vuelvan tus padres” — antes de que always takes the subjunctive vuelvan.

exercises.prompt: No pienso moverme de aquí hasta que me lo ___. (explicar, tú)
exercises.prompt_en: I don't intend to move from here until you explain it to me.
exercises.hint: hasta que + an action still to come → subjunctive of explicar.
exercises.no: The explanation hasn't happened yet, so hasta que needs the subjunctive: “expliques”.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence half to its correct verb form.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Realizado o habitual → indicativo; pendiente → subjuntivo.

exercises.tts: Una vez que hayas firmado, te enviaré el contrato.
accepted: una vez que hayas firmado te enviare el contrato
exercises.translation: Once you've signed, I'll send you the contract.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Una vez que hayas firmado, te enviaré el contrato.”
exercises.no: It was: “Una vez que hayas firmado, te enviaré el contrato.” (Once you've signed, I'll send you the contract.)

lines.speaker: Repartidor
lines.es: No estaré en casa toda la mañana. ¿Cómo quedamos con el paquete?
lines.en: I won't be home all morning. How shall we handle the parcel?

options.text: Déjelo con el portero en cuanto llegue el mensajero.
Déjelo con el portero en cuanto llega el mensajero.
Déjelo con el portero en cuanto llegará el mensajero.

exercises.no: The courier's arrival is still to come, so use the subjunctive: “en cuanto llegue”.

exercises.en: We'll talk when you have a moment.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Hablamos cuando tengas un momento.”
